projects.name: Analytics Dashboard
projects.description:
An analytics dashboard that ingests and processes customer CSV files, analyzes application logs, and presents insights through visualization components. Scope spans three data domains (customer CSV processing, application log analysis, visualization/UI) plus the shared platform work needed to connect them.

Tags: analytics, dashboard, data-processing, logs, visualization

tasks.name: M1: Foundation & Data Architecture
tasks.details: Establish the technical foundation every data domain depends on: repository scaffolding, canonical data schemas, a storage/warehouse layer, and configuration/secrets handling. Exit criteria: a running skeleton service, documented schemas for customer and log data, and a working connection to the target data store.

tasks.name: M2: Customer CSV Ingestion & Processing
tasks.details: Build the pipeline that takes raw customer CSV files and turns them into clean, queryable customer records. Covers file intake, schema validation, cleaning/normalization, deduplication, and load into the warehouse. Exit criteria: an end-to-end run that loads a sample CSV batch and produces a validated customer table with a data-quality report.

tasks.name: M3: Application Log Analysis Pipeline
tasks.details: Build the pipeline that parses application logs, extracts structured events, and computes operational metrics (error rates, latency, request volume, top failure modes). Exit criteria: log files flow through parsing into aggregated metric tables that the dashboard can query by time window and service.

tasks.name: M4: Visualization & Dashboard UI
tasks.details: Deliver the user-facing dashboard: query API over the processed data, a component library, and the actual dashboard views for customer and log analytics. Exit criteria: a user can open the dashboard, filter by date range, and see charts populated from real processed data.

tasks.name: M5: Integration, Testing & Deployment
tasks.details: Harden and ship: automated test coverage across pipelines and UI, scheduled orchestration of both data pipelines, monitoring/alerting, and deployment to a target environment. Exit criteria: CI runs green, pipelines run on a schedule, and the dashboard is reachable in a staging environment with alerting configured.

tasks.name: Scaffold repository and local dev environment
tasks.details: Create the monorepo/service skeleton: language runtime, dependency manifest, linting/formatting, folder layout for ingestion, analysis, and UI packages, plus a one-command local start script and README with setup steps. Acceptance: a fresh clone can install and run the empty service locally.

tasks.name: Define canonical customer data schema
tasks.details: Document field-level contract for customer records: column names, types, required vs optional, nullability, value ranges, and enums for customer status/segment. Include a sample anonymized CSV fixture and write the schema as executable validation rules (e.g. JSON Schema / Pydantic / dbt contract). Acceptance: schema file reviewed and accepted, sample fixture passes validation.

tasks.name: Define application log event schema
tasks.details: Collect 3-5 representative real log samples, identify formats in use (JSON lines, plaintext, multi-line stack traces), and define the normalized event contract: timestamp, service, severity, request_id, latency_ms, status_code, message, error_type. Document parsing assumptions and unmapped fields. Acceptance: schema documented; samples collected into a test fixture directory.

tasks.name: Provision data store and connectivity layer
tasks.details: Stand up the target analytical store (warehouse or Postgres + a lightweight aggregation store, per team preference), create raw/staging/curated layers or schemas, and implement a single shared connection/database client module with retry and connection pooling. Acceptance: smoke-test query succeeds against all three layers from the app code.

tasks.name: Set up configuration and secrets management
tasks.details: Add environment-based config loading with validation on startup, a checked-in .env.example, secret handling for DB credentials and any API keys, and clear failure messages when required config is missing. Acceptance: app fails fast with an actionable error on missing config and loads correctly from .env.

tasks.name: Build CSV file intake handler
tasks.details: Implement discovery and intake of customer CSV files from the agreed source (upload endpoint or watched directory): encode detection (UTF-8/Latin-1), delimiter sniffing, header normalization, and idempotent tracking of already-processed files by checksum. Acceptance: drop-in test of 3 differently formatted CSVs all register correctly without duplicate reprocessing.

tasks.name: Implement CSV validation and bad-row quarantine
tasks.details: Apply the canonical customer schema to each row, collect structured validation errors (row number, field, reason), route rejects into a quarantine table/file, and report counts of accepted vs rejected rows. Do not fail the whole batch on individual bad rows. Acceptance: a CSV with intentional bad rows loads the good rows and quarantines only the bad ones with readable reasons.

tasks.name: Implement cleaning and normalization transforms
tasks.details: Trim whitespace, normalize casing, coerce types, standardize dates to ISO-8601 UTC, normalize country codes and phone formats, map free-text status/segment values to the canonical enums, and default safe values where allowed. Keep transforms pure functions so they are unit-testable. Acceptance: unit tests cover each transform with before/after cases.

tasks.name: Implement customer deduplication and identity merge
tasks.details: Define the match key (e.g. normalized email primary, fuzzy name+phone secondary), implement matching against existing warehouse records, pick a deterministic survivor record with deterministic field-level priority for conflicts, and log merge decisions to an audit table. Acceptance: a fixture with known duplicates collapses to the expected record count with merges traceable.

tasks.name: Build idempotent warehouse load job
tasks.details: Write curated customer records into the warehouse customer table using an upsert keyed on the surrogate customer id, wrapped in a transaction or staged swap so a failed run leaves the prior state intact. Add a job run record (source file, row counts, duration, status). Acceptance: re-running the same batch twice produces no duplicate rows.

tasks.name: Generate customer data-quality report
tasks.details: Produce a per-run quality summary: rows read/accepted/rejected, null-rate per required field, enum violations, duplicate rate, and freshness timestamp. Render it to a simple markdown/HTML artifact and expose the same numbers via a service method the dashboard can later consume. Acceptance: report generated automatically at end of every pipeline run.

tasks.name: Build log collection and rotation-aware reader
tasks.details: Implement a reader that handles the log source layout (app log files, rotated archives, optionally a container log dir), tracks read offsets so restarts do not re-read or skip lines, and tolerates files being rotated mid-read. Acceptance: reader resumes correctly across a simulated rotation and restart with zero duplicated or missing lines.

tasks.name: Implement log parser for JSON and plaintext formats
tasks.details: Build the parser that turns raw lines into the normalized event contract: JSON-lines fast path, regex fallback for plaintext, and continuation-line handling to reassemble multi-line stack traces into a single event. Unparseable lines go to a dead-letter bucket with the raw line preserved. Acceptance: parser correctly normalizes all fixture formats and reports a parse success rate.

tasks.name: Add error classification and event enrichment
tasks.details: Derive an error_type/error_category from exception names and message patterns, extract endpoint names, user/session identifiers where present, and severity normalization across formats. Include a small versioned mapping table so categories can be tuned without code changes. Acceptance: a labelled sample of 50 log events classifies with agreed accuracy and mappings are editable in config.

tasks.name: Implement log aggregation metrics job
tasks.details: Compute per-service, per-hour rollups: request volume, error count and error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, top 10 error categories, and unique-session counts. Write to an aggregate metrics table keyed by (service, hour) with an idempotent replace-window strategy. Acceptance: rollups match hand-computed expected values on a fixture dataset.

tasks.name: Add PII scrubbing and log retention policy
tasks.details: Redact emails, tokens, IPs, and auth headers from parsed messages before persistence, and implement a configurable retention window with a purge job that drops raw log rows past the policy while keeping aggregates. Acceptance: redaction tests pass on PII fixtures and the purge job removes only rows older than the configured window.

tasks.name: Build shared query layer with filters and caching
tasks.details: Create the single data-access layer the UI calls: date-range and service/segment filter parsing and validation, parameterized SQL (no string concatenation), result pagination, and a short-TTL cache keyed on the normalized query. Acceptance: invalid filters return clean 400s and repeated identical queries hit cache.

tasks.name: Build customer analytics API endpoints
tasks.details: Expose read endpoints for customer metrics: totals and growth over time, breakdown by segment/status/region, and data-quality summary from the latest pipeline run. Each returns a stable typed response contract with a documented shape. Acceptance: endpoint contract tests pass and responses match warehouse values.

tasks.name: Build operational metrics API endpoints
tasks.details: Expose read endpoints over the log aggregates: error-rate and request-volume time series, latency percentiles, top error categories, and a latest-events feed. Support the same shared filter/pagination layer and cap time-series bucket counts. Acceptance: endpoint contract tests pass and series align with the aggregation job output.

tasks.name: Build reusable chart component library
tasks.details: Implement a small set of accessible wrappers over the charting library: line/time-series, bar, stacked bar, KPI stat card, and data table. Each handles loading, empty, and error states consistently and accepts a typed data prop. Acceptance: a component playground/story renders every component with mock data plus loading and empty states.

tasks.name: Assemble customer analytics dashboard view
tasks.details: Compose the customer view from the component library and customer endpoints: KPI row, growth chart, segment breakdown, and quality panel. Wire the global date-range filter to the view and add drill-down from a segment to a filtered customer table. Acceptance: view renders real data end-to-end and filter changes update every panel.

tasks.name: Assemble application health dashboard view
tasks.details: Compose the operational view: error-rate and volume time series, latency percentile chart, top-error-category bar chart, and recent-events table. Share the global date-range filter and add a service selector. Acceptance: view renders real aggregate data and both filters drive every panel.

tasks.name: Add dashboard shell, navigation, and responsive layout
tasks.details: Build the app shell: navigation between views, persisted global filters, responsive grid that collapses to single column on narrow screens, and consistent empty/error/no-data states. Acceptance: both views are reachable and usable at desktop and mobile widths with no layout breakage.

tasks.name: Write unit tests for transforms and parsers
tasks.details: Cover CSV cleaning/normalization functions, validation rules, dedup match logic, log parsing branches, and error classification with table-driven tests against the fixture datasets. Target meaningful coverage of branching logic rather than a raw percentage. Acceptance: suite runs fast locally and fails clearly on a deliberately broken assertion.

tasks.name: Build end-to-end pipeline integration test harness
tasks.details: Create a disposable test database plus golden fixtures (a customer CSV batch and a log batch) and a single test that runs intake through load, then asserts expected warehouse and aggregate row counts and a handful of key values. Acceptance: the full pipeline passes in CI against a clean database in one command.

tasks.name: Add dashboard component and smoke tests
tasks.details: Add rendering tests for each chart component covering data, loading, empty, and error states, plus a smoke test that mounts each dashboard view with mocked API responses and asserts key panels render. Acceptance: tests catch a deliberately broken component and run headless in CI.

tasks.name: Set up pipeline orchestration and scheduling
tasks.details: Wire both pipelines into a scheduler (cron or workflow engine) with dependency ordering (CSV load and log aggregation independent; metrics rollup after log parse), retry with backoff, concurrency lock so a run cannot overlap itself, and run-history records. Acceptance: two consecutive scheduled runs complete with visible history and no overlap.

tasks.name: Configure CI pipeline for lint, tests, and build
tasks.details: Add a CI workflow that runs lint, type checks, unit tests, integration tests against a service container database, and a production build of the dashboard on every push and PR, with dependency caching. Acceptance: a green run on the main branch and a red run on a deliberately failing branch.

tasks.name: Add pipeline monitoring and alerting
tasks.details: Emit structured run logs plus key metrics (run duration, rows processed, reject rate, freshness lag), add health endpoints for API and DB, and configure two alerts: pipeline failure and data-staleness beyond threshold. Acceptance: a forced failure and a simulated stale dataset each trigger the correct alert.

tasks.name: Deploy to staging and write operations runbook
tasks.details: Add a container build and staging deployment (config via env, migrations applied on release), then document the runbook: how to deploy, roll back, re-run a failed pipeline, query the warehouse, and where alerts land. Acceptance: a clean deploy reaches a working staging URL and an engineer not on the project can follow the runbook unaided.
